notes: Collected via outlet RSS (Science X category feeds, SciAm, DeepMind, GEN, Physics World, Psychology Today, Live Science, TQI, UT, Quanta, STAT, MIT TR) + 32 Google News RSS when:14d discovery queries across the full keyword set; 2 WebSearch used (astronomy, quantum gaps — yielded only stale/already-published items). Science X (phys.org/techxplore/medicalxpress) HTML is 403 to curl: bodies via WebFetch, times from outlet RSS pubDate. Outlet cap <=3 applied (phys.org, techxplore, medicalxpress each 3 in main set + 1 phys.org/medx alternate beyond cap noted). Keyword expansion used: percolation theory/LLM proofs, protein watermarking/biosecurity provenance, chromatin imaging aging, geospatial ecology AI, LLM social norms, knowledge collapse, LLM uncertainty. Dropped: spin-glass quantum AI memory (9/3 stale), AI-physics-experiments (already in ledger), AI-industry noise (OpenAI/Anthropic/Nvidia/AMD/IPO), STAT+ policy (paywall/policy), Terra Quantum laser welding (industrial). No astronomy/particle/quantum AI item fresh and unpublished in window. Per-outlet cap trimmed: phys.org Change.org petitions and medicalxpress gut-microbiome AI kept out as over-cap alternates.

items.headline: AI scientist autonomously generates and validates new biological discoveries
items.excerpt: Chalmers researchers combined LLMs, automated reasoning and lab robotics into a closed-loop AI scientist that generates hypotheses, runs experiments on brewer's yeast and interprets results (J. R. Soc. Interface).

items.headline: AI solves a 'holy grail' problem from probability theory
items.excerpt: Days after Fields Medalist Hugo Duminil-Copin predicted it, Anthropic released an LLM-generated proof of a long-standing percolation-theory conjecture on the critical threshold.

items.headline: Introducing SynthID Bio
items.excerpt: DeepMind's SynthID Bio embeds imperceptible watermarks into AI-designed protein sequences and AlphaFold 3 structures; wet-lab tests show watermarked binders keep hit rate and affinity.

items.headline: Physics-grounded AI framework aims to make predictions about new materials more testable
items.excerpt: Tohoku's PhysMat AI perspective (Adv. Funct. Mater.) builds physical knowledge into materials-discovery AI as priors, descriptors, constraints, verifiers and infrastructure.

items.headline: Drones, satellites and AI help scientists watch over Antarctica's smallest lifeforms
items.excerpt: UOW-led geospatial AI framework links ground surveys, drone imagery and satellite data to map Antarctic moss, lichen and cyanobacteria across scales over seven years.

items.headline: Helping 'bad' people drew disapproval from some of 21 AI models
items.excerpt: PNAS Nexus study probes the social norms of 21 LLMs judging cooperation with people of good or bad reputation; most drift toward 'Simple Standing'.

items.headline: AI detects signs of aging in blood stem cells from nuclear images
items.excerpt: IDIBELL/BSC's ChromAgeNet CNN reads 3D chromatin organization in DAPI-stained hematopoietic stem cell nuclei to classify young vs aged cells (77%), Aging Cell.

items.headline: Machine learning toolkit can improve odds of drug development success
items.excerpt: SwRI's GAMES uses LLMs to generate molecular strings ranked against FDA-approved drug properties; identified 18 antiviral candidates for filovirus treatment.

items.headline: AI chatbots give us a narrow slice of knowledge: Researchers warn of 'knowledge collapse'
items.excerpt: Copenhagen study of 27 LLMs over 155 topics (~70M claims) finds even GPT-5 gives at least 18.7% less varied information than Google (EMNLP 2026).

items.headline: Quantum-inspired math could help AI recognize when it does not know the answer
items.excerpt: University of Miami framework uses quantum-inspired math and a missing-species model to flag LLM uncertainty (ICLR).

items.headline: Turning to AI for health answers may signal anxiety, depression among young adults
items.excerpt: University of Florida study: young adults who ask generative AI health questions more likely to screen positive for anxiety and depression.

items.headline: Did OpenAI solve the wrong Navier-Stokes problem?
items.excerpt: OpenAI's LLM-generated Navier-Stokes proof relies on an external-force loophole; mathematicians say the core problem stays open.

items.headline: AI and Proteomics Accelerate VAV1 Molecular Glue Discovery
items.excerpt: Baylor's GluePlex workflow plus proteomics finds VAV1-degrading molecular glues (Nature Communications).

items.headline: Google DeepMind's latest AI tool promises a new era for genetics research
items.excerpt: Live Science on DeepMind's AlphaGenome Atlas variant-effect map; experts urge caution.

items.headline: Drones, AI and the future of wildlife conservation
items.excerpt: Physics World piece on drones and AI analysis for wildlife monitoring and conservation.

items.headline: Do We Still Have Agency When AI Helps Us Decide?
items.excerpt: Psychology Today blog on human agency and decision-making with AI assistance.
